# Calab — full description

> Calab is a voice-first team messenger you can run on your own server: always-open voice rooms, video and screen sharing, Telegram-style chat, a calendar with meetings, task boards, notes, phone calls over SIP, workspace web apps, and bots with an API and SDK. Desktop apps for macOS, Windows and Linux, plus a web app that also works on phones.

This file is the detailed version of https://calab.io/llms.txt. It describes only what exists in the product today; things that are planned are listed separately at the end and are marked as not available. Site: https://calab.io (languages: /en/, /ru/, /es/, /zh/). Source: https://github.com/itrcz/calab. Contact: it@gptunnel.ai. A Russian summary is at the very end.

## What Calab is

Calab is a team messenger where voice comes first. You join a room and hear your colleagues right away; next to it are a Telegram-style chat, a calendar with meetings and Linear-style task boards. Everything runs on your own server: one `docker compose`, with PostgreSQL and LiveKit inside and no external services or subscriptions required.

- Clients: desktop app (Electron) for macOS (Apple Silicon and Intel, signed and notarized), Windows 10/11 (the installer is not code-signed yet, so SmartScreen shows "Unknown publisher" on first launch) and Linux (AppImage and .deb, x64). A web app works in Chrome, Edge, Safari and Firefox, adapts to phones and installs to the home screen. The desktop app updates itself.
- Server: Go, PostgreSQL (17 or 18), Valkey/Redis, LiveKit for media, Caddy for TLS and the single public entry point.
- Target size of the current version: teams of up to 20–30 people online at once and up to three screen shares per room. Horizontal scaling is on the roadmap of the project; a rough sizing for a 30-person team is about 4 vCPUs and 8 GB of RAM.
- Interface languages: Russian, English, Spanish and Chinese on the site; the app itself is localized as well.

## Voice rooms, video, screen sharing

- Voice rooms are always open: one click to join; who is talking is visible right in the room list; rooms show a status, a timer and a member limit.
- Voice activation or push-to-talk on any key, including in the background (global hotkeys in the desktop app).
- Echo cancellation (AEC3) and optional RNNoise noise suppression, both running in the client with no external services. Opus with DTX. A musician mode turns all processing off for live instruments and singing (Team and above). Remote audio is played through a plain audio element, which is what keeps echo cancellation working.
- Screen sharing in AV1 or hardware H.264 with simulcast: each viewer receives the quality their connection allows. Viewers can point and draw on top of the stream. Any window can be shared. Screen-share sound is sent unprocessed, and the other participants' voices stay out of the stream (macOS 14.2+, Windows 11).
- Camera with background blur or a picture (built-in and workspace backgrounds).
- One-on-one calls in direct messages, with ringing, camera and screen sharing.
- Soundboard: sounds (built-in plus workspace sounds uploaded by admins) played to everyone in the room; each client plays the clip locally, so the voice track is never degraded.
- Moderation: server-side mute, disconnect, move a participant to another room by drag and drop; statuses.
- Temporary rooms: a room for an hour or a day that any member can create (name, lifetime, visible to everyone or only to chosen people), with a guest link ready immediately and an optional calendar meeting. Expired rooms cannot be joined and stay in the archive. This covers quick calls with customers without a separate conferencing tool.
- Recording and transcripts: the server records a meeting, the workspace's GPTunneL connection transcribes it, and a card with the summary, the audio and the full transcript arrives in the room chat. The workspace connects to GPTunneL once, with a code in the settings; the audio is kept as the card's attachment for 30 days; recording can be disabled in the room settings. Guests cannot record.

## Audio quality

Each room sets its own audio quality level (Opus, mono):

| Level | Bitrate | Audio band |
|---|---|---|
| Low | 8 kbps | up to 4 kHz |
| Normal | 16 kbps | up to 8 kHz |
| Good | 32 kbps | up to 12 kHz |
| Excellent | 64 kbps | up to 20 kHz (full band) |

- The default is 32 kbps; everyone can set a personal ceiling to save data on a worse connection.
- While the microphone is silent a voice uses about 0.1 kbps (DTX). Typical traffic: voice 16–64 kbps per speaker; a static screen share 20–300 kbps, capped at 2 Mbps for 1080p.
- RNNoise is optional; while it is off, Chromium's built-in suppression works.
- The Free plan is limited to the "Normal" level; Team and above can use any level.
- Musician mode: a personal toggle for playing an instrument or singing live. It turns off echo cancellation, noise suppression and auto gain for the microphone and sends audio in the Opus music profile: 128 kbps mono or 192 kbps stereo, with forward error correction and without DTX. Headphones are required (the app warns about it), because without echo cancellation loudspeaker sound returns to other participants. Others see a guitar icon next to your name. Available on Team, Business and Enterprise; on Free the option is visible with a lock.

## Chat

- Every room has its own chat. Replies, reactions, forwarding to several chats at once, stickers (workspace sticker packs, static and animated WebP), voice messages, files with previews and a built-in player for music and video, pins, read ticks.
- Mentions, per-room notifications, an inbox of unread mentions, workspace search with morphology, a Cmd/Ctrl+K quick switcher.
- Direct messages with an archive.
- A task link unfolds into a card in the chat; a task can be created from any message.

## Calendar and meetings

- A day view with meetings side by side, a "now" line, the meeting card with attendees and their answers, the room with a "Go" button, recurring meetings and reminders 15 minutes before.
- Invitations by email with an `invite.ics` attachment: the meeting lands in Apple, Google, Outlook or Yandex calendars. External attendees answer by link and join as guests.
- Find a time: colleagues' busy columns, shared free windows and the nearest slots within everyone's work hours; one click creates the meeting.
- CalDAV: connect a Yandex, iCloud, Fastmail or Nextcloud calendar with an app password. Your busy time counts when colleagues look for a time, external events appear in your day (with title, place and attendees, and a "Create a Calab meeting" button), and your Calab meetings appear there by themselves. Colleagues see your external calendar as busy only, with a title, or with title and attendees, depending on your setting. CalDAV is available on Team, Business and Enterprise.

## Task boards and approvals

- Kanban, list and timeline (Gantt with milestones and a "today" line), in the spirit of Linear and with its keyboard shortcuts.
- Statuses, priorities, labels, milestones, due dates; several assignees with a lead, subtasks and relations; task keys like `FNG-12`.
- Comments work like chat (reactions, stickers, voice messages) and are mixed with the change history; the activity feed has tabs All / Changes / Comments.
- Filters, saved views, bulk actions, drag and drop of cards between columns.
- Approvals: assign approvers and the number of approvals needed (all, or N of M). An approver approves, or rejects with a comment (a veto); a decision can be withdrawn. Until a task is approved it cannot move further along the board, and editing the title or description restarts approval.
- Access to a board is by roles and people, like rooms; boards can be private or closed even to administrators (see Roles).
- Board limits by plan: Free 3, Team 30, Business 50, Enterprise unlimited.

## Notes

Up to 20 private shelves per person with their own names and emoji, like "Saved Messages" in Telegram, only several. Drag messages and files onto a shelf, forward to it, pin and search. Only the owner sees a shelf.

## Guests

- A guest link leads straight into a room, no sign-up: the guest types a name and joins. A guest sees only their room.
- Approval ("waiting room"): per room or per link, the guest waits on a screen until the organizer clicks "Let in"; the organizer sees a waiting counter and a sound, and can rename the guest, give a badge, let in or decline.
- Calendar meetings give external attendees guest links that inherit the room's setting.

## Web apps

An admin pins site shortcuts (Grafana, a wiki, a CRM) under the workspace icon in the left rail: a picture, a name and an address, up to 20 per workspace. A click opens the site inside Calab, full window, and the call keeps going. Logins are kept separately for each app and never mix with Calab. Camera and microphone for a site are available only with your permission. Order is changed by drag and drop. Everyone except guests sees the apps; people with the integrations permission add and change them. A hidden app that uses more than 2 % of a core is unloaded after 15 seconds (its session and logins stay). In the desktop app the site opens in an isolated view; in the web app it opens in a sandboxed frame, and sites that forbid embedding are offered in a new tab (on a phone the app opens in a new tab right away).

## Phone calls (SIP)

- Connect your own SIP provider (server, port, transport, login, password, Caller ID, dialling prefix, allowed destination prefixes) in workspace settings, "Telephony". The provider bills the calls.
- From a voice room, "Call a number" (room header and the "..." menu) dials a landline or mobile number; paste the number as it is. The callee joins the room as a participant with a phone icon, everyone hears them, and the status is visible to all: dialling, ringing, on the call with a timer. The caller and moderators can hang up; only the caller hears the ringback.
- "Test connection" places a short trial call to your Caller ID; a call log shows who called, when, where and how it ended.
- The "Place calls" permission is given to nobody by default. Limits: one call per room, up to 20 calls an hour per workspace, 2 hours at most per call; destinations can be limited by prefix (for example +7). Guests cannot place calls.
- Technically this uses LiveKit's SIP service in a container enabled by a flag on your server, so echo cancellation and recording work for phone participants like for people. Outgoing calls only at the moment.

## Bots, API, SDK, webhooks

- A bot is a workspace member with a token (`calab_bot_…`); it uses the same REST API and realtime gateway as the app, with rights coming from roles. A bot sees only rooms and boards it is allowed to see; closed rooms and boards apply to bots too.
- It can read and write chat in rooms and DMs, reply, react, send files and stickers, register `/commands` (suggested in the composer), and attach buttons under messages (up to 5 rows of 5; a press reaches only that bot as an event).
- Tasks: create, edit, comment, assign, search.
- Voice: a bot joins a voice room through LiveKit (Node, Python, Go), hears participants and speaks (text to speech, echo, music, recording).
- Bot API v2: calendar (create, move and cancel meetings as the organizer, free/busy, find a time), member profiles with open tasks, renaming, invitations by link and email, badges and sounds, guest admission, starting and stopping meeting recording.
- Events arrive over a WebSocket gateway or as a webhook: a POST with an HMAC-SHA256 signature, retries with backoff for up to a day, and dedupe by delivery id.
- Limits: 30 requests per second per bot, 20 messages per minute, messages up to 4000 characters. The number of bots depends on the plan.
- TypeScript SDK (`@calaba/bot-sdk`), examples (echo, voice echo, text to speech, Python) in the repository.

```ts
import { Bot } from '@calaba/bot-sdk';

const bot = new Bot(process.env.BOT_TOKEN, { server: 'https://app.calab.io' });
bot.on('message', (m) => bot.reply(m, m.content));
await bot.start();
```

Docs: https://github.com/itrcz/calab/blob/main/docs/19-bot-api.en.md (English), https://github.com/itrcz/calab/blob/main/docs/19-bot-api.md (Russian). Landing page: https://calab.io/en/bots/. SDK: https://github.com/itrcz/calab/tree/main/packages/bot-sdk. Examples: https://github.com/itrcz/calab/tree/main/examples/bots.

## Roles and permissions

- Rights are a bitmask computed by one function, identically on the server (Go) and in the client (TypeScript), with shared test vectors. Every right is checked on the server; the LiveKit grant mirrors the rights; the client only hides UI.
- Multiple roles per member, per-room and per-board overrides for roles and for people.
- Roles v2: separate rights per function instead of one "manage workspace": create boards, manage members (kick, ban, badges, role assignment), manage bots, manage integrations (SIP, GPTunneL), view journals (call log, board activity), manage events, manage recordings; separate rights to invite members and to invite guests.
- Private rooms and boards are visible only to a list of people; "closed" rooms and boards are not visible even to administrators (only the workspace owner sees everything). Objects a user cannot see answer "not found", so their existence is not revealed.

## Performance

Measurements are published with their method in docs/14-energy.md (https://github.com/itrcz/calab/blob/main/docs/14-energy.md). Machine: MacBook Air (Apple M4, 10 cores, 24 GB), macOS 27, Discord 0.0.413. CPU is the sum over all processes of the app, as a percentage of one core, sampled every 5 seconds for 3 minutes, one run per scenario.

- Without a call: Calab 0.05 % CPU with the window visible and 0.2 % with the window hidden; Discord on the same Mac, back to back in the same conditions: 0.97 % and 0.85 %.
- In voice with a quiet room: about 7 % (6.9 %, down from 15.0 % before RNNoise started running on demand). The project's own budget is 5 %, which is not met yet.
- A hidden window no longer decodes video: 7.0 %, down from 17.5 %.
- Solid materials instead of glass and blur (no backdrop-filter); the recording indicator pulses three times instead of blinking for hours; the macOS installer lost 16.3 MB of unused Chromium languages.
- We did not measure Discord in a call, so we make no voice comparison. Numbers are for one machine and will differ on others.
- Rules inside the product: no backdrop-filter, no infinite animations except loaders, a hidden window does not decode video or run timers, a low-power mode for weak computers.

## Security and self-hosting

- Media: DTLS-SRTP. API and signaling: HTTPS/WSS, HSTS, strict CSP. Web sessions use HttpOnly, SameSite=Strict cookies; passwords are hashed with argon2id; refresh tokens rotate with reuse detection; rate limits. There is no end-to-end encryption yet: media goes through your own media server.
- Works behind VPNs and firewalls: UDP, then ICE/TCP, then TURN/UDP 443, then TURN/TLS on 443, automatically; one public IP is enough.
- Install: a Linux host with a public IP, Docker with Compose and a domain with A records for `app`, `rtc` and `turn` (and `@` for the site). Clone the repository, copy `infra/docker/.env.example` to `infra/docker/.env`, run `infra/docker/deploy.sh`. Ports: 80/443 TCP, 443/UDP, 7881/TCP, 7882/UDP. The first registered user becomes the server owner; others join by invitation. Let's Encrypt certificates are automatic, containers are hardened, backups run daily with a verified restore, Prometheus metrics are exposed. Files can be stored on disk or in any S3-compatible bucket.
- Guide: https://github.com/itrcz/calab/blob/main/docs/06-deployment.md. Security reports: it@gptunnel.ai (https://github.com/itrcz/calab/blob/main/SECURITY.md).

## Plans

Free, Team and Business are cloud plans of a workspace; Enterprise is Calab on your own server, without limits. Limits are enforced on the server. Global (Unne L.L.C-FZ): Team USD $0.10 and Business USD $0.30 per employee per complete rolling 24 hours, base prices excluding applicable taxes; the final total is shown before payment. RU (ООО «Громтех»): Team 6 RUB and Business 18 RUB per employee per 24 hours, without VAT. The owner counts; guests, bots and pending invitations do not. Balance top-ups fund daily seat charges, with optional automatic top-up. Current teams can run a negative balance for up to seven days without increasing paid capacity, then service and accrual stop. No monthly/yearly commitment or discount. Payments are being prepared for launch; contact support@calab.io. Free is free; Enterprise is free for non-commercial use, commercial licence on request.

Global paid terms: https://calab.io/en/legal/offer/; EULA: https://calab.io/en/legal/terms/; privacy: https://calab.io/en/legal/privacy/. RU documents: https://calab.io/ru/legal/offer/. The marketing site has no active analytics/advertising trackers; optional language storage is controlled in the corner preferences panel. Cookie policy: https://calab.io/en/legal/cookies/.

| | Free | Team | Business | Enterprise (own server) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| People in a voice room | 5 | 15 | 50 | unlimited |
| Workspace members | 50 | 100 | 500 | unlimited |
| Files | 5 GB | 300 GB | 1 TB | unlimited |
| Bots | 1 | 5 | 20 | unlimited |

| Support | none | yes | priority | yes |

Also: Free is limited to the "Normal" audio level and to 720p / 15 fps for screen sharing and camera; Team and above have no quality limits. Sticker packs: 1 on Free, unlimited above. The calendar is on every plan. Guests do not count as members. Details: https://calab.io/en/#pricing.

## Planned, not available yet

These are on the roadmap. Do not present them as existing features.

- Voice AI assistant: a voice AI assistant in rooms. It is already in testing and is not generally available.
- IVR: a voice menu and internal extension numbers for phone calls (SIP).
- Wiki: a team knowledge base.
- Disk: shared file storage for the workspace.

## Кратко по-русски

Calab — голосовой (voice-first) мессенджер для команды, который ставится на ваш сервер. Голосовые комнаты, видео и показ экрана, запись встреч с расшифровкой и резюме, чат как в Telegram, личные сообщения и звонки один на один, календарь (приглашения .ics, «Подобрать время», CalDAV), доски задач (канбан, список, таймлайн, согласование задач), заметки, гости с подтверждением входа, временные комнаты, звонки на городские и мобильные номера через SIP (нужен свой SIP-провайдер), веб-приложения пространства в левой панели, боты с API v2, SDK и вебхуками, роли по функциям и закрытые разделы. Приложения для macOS, Windows, Linux и веб-версия. Нагрузка: 0,05 % процессора без звонка и около 7 % в голосе на MacBook Air M4 (замеры и метод — docs/14-energy.md; сравнения голоса с Discord нет). Сквозного шифрования пока нет. Лицензия BSL 1.1, через четыре года версия переходит на Apache 2.0. Тарифы: Free, Team, Business (облако) и Enterprise (свой сервер): человек в голосовой комнате 5 / 15 / 50 / без ограничений, участников 50 / 100 / 500 / без ограничений, файлы 5 ГБ / 300 ГБ / 1 ТБ / без ограничений, боты 1 / 5 / 20, доски 3 / 30 / 50, одновременных стримов в комнате 1 / 2 / 5, камер 3 / 10 / 25, CalDAV и режим музыканта (звук без обработки, Opus 128/192 кбит/с, значок гитары) со второго тарифа, поддержка: Team — есть, Business — приоритетная, Enterprise — есть. В планах (пока нет): голосовой ИИ-ассистент (уже тестируется), IVR и внутренние номера, Wiki, Диск. Сайт: https://calab.io/ru/, контакт: it@gptunnel.ai.

## Workspace identity (Identity 2.0)

Business and Enterprise include employee sign-in via OpenID Connect (SSO), LDAPS synchronization of linked members’ status and direct Active Directory groups, and OAuth 2.0 / OpenID Connect for signing into your applications with Calab. Register OAuth clients in workspace settings; users consent to sharing a minimal profile. These clients do not grant access to the chat API.

Open SSO settings in your workspace to connect an OpenID Connect provider and an LDAPS directory, or OAuth clients to register an application with redirect URIs. Active Business or activated Enterprise access is required. Accounts are linked explicitly, never automatically by matching email. Directory sync does not create users or process nested groups.
